summary: This witness began observing the log at tree size 580. Everything it can prove dates from here: it has nothing to compare an earlier state against.
how_to_verify: Each head below carries signed_payload: the exact bytes the log signed, as RFC 8785 canonical JSON. No BurnLedger code is needed to rebuild it.

Verify with any Ed25519 implementation: ed25519_verify(public_key=pinned_keys[i].public_key, message=signed_payload, signature=head.signature). All three fields are hex except signed_payload, which is the literal text.
Worked example (python3, package 'cryptography', run against THIS file): deploy/WITNESS-THIRD-PARTY.md, section 'Verifying an evidence record yourself'. It depends on nothing from BurnLedger.

Two heads with the SAME tree_size and DIFFERENT root_hash, both verifying, are proof of equivocation: an append-only log cannot have had two states at one size. This holds forever and does not require trusting the witness, its host, or the log operator.
A head whose signature_verifies is false proves nothing about the operator on its own — it records only what this witness was served.
